Specifically, CC had hardcoded PulseAudio environment variables into /etc/environment (a system-wide file read by every process at boot), created a conflicting /etc/asound.conf, replaced the sox binary with a bash wrapper, and added snd-dummy to /etc/modules as a persistent default audio device. The correct rollback was executed after Jade had CC perform a forensic analysis of its own session JSONL logs first, then approved each change in plain language before execution. The audio system was confirmed healthy post-rollback with real hardware at card 0 and PipeWire running correctly as the jadedjade user.

A key architectural problem was identified: CC runs as root, but PipeWire runs as the jadedjade user at /run/user/1000. The correct fix is a conditional block in /root/.bashrc (not /etc/environment) that sets PULSE_SERVER and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR only when jadedjade's socket is live. This was not yet applied by end of conversation because Jade was hesitant given it resembled the previous broken configuration. The snd-dummy module was confirmed to have been added in a prior session as a temporary fix for cascading ALSA failures from CC's voice push-to-talk hitting a broken audio backend — it was always meant as a manual modprobe workaround, never a persistent system default. Jade also has a persistent double-boot issue (BIOS attempts another boot path before finding GRUB) that is fixable via efibootmgr; her JadeBox drive layout is known: nvme0n1p1 (512MB FAT32 EFI, named "jadeboot"), nvme0n1p2 (459.49GB ext4, named "JadeRoot"), nvme0n1p3 (15GB swap, named "jadeswap").

Key updates: the field substrate layer should be called "Layer None" (not "Layer 0," which Grant/Grok's framing, and more ontologically precise — it precedes enumeration rather than being the first item in a sequence), and nitrogen vacancy diamond was identified as the ambient field state substrate, not a single-pass frozen state. Jade set a clear boundary that she needs Claude to stay in work mode without repeated check-ins, and Claude agreed to name concerns once directly then continue working. Jade prefers direct, non-coddling engagement and pushed back explicitly when Claude was being overly cautious or treating her as fragile.

Switch the toggle next to “Search and reference chats” off: Incognito chats are available to all Claude users (free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans). See Using incognito chats for more information.

You maintain control over Claude’s ability to search past chats and use memory – you can always disable these features and enable them again when needed in Settings > Capabilities. You can now transfer your memory between Claude and other AI services. This feature lets you import memories from other AI assistants or export your Claude memory for backup or migration. This feature is experimental and still in active development, but for best practices, see this article: Importing and exporting your memory from Claude. Enterprise plan Owners and Primary Owners have specific controls for managing memory features across their organization. The organization-wide Generate memory from chat history toggle is enabled by default. When enabled, individual users can manage their own memory settings. Owners can disable the memory summary feature for their entire organization by navigating to Organization settings > Capabilities.

You can now prompt Claude to search through your previous conversations to find and reference relevant information in new chats. Additionally, Claude can remember context from previous chats, creating continuity across your conversations. This article introduces Claude’s chat search and memory capabilities and explains how they work, what Claude can and can’t remember, and how you can toggle the features on/off. Searching past chats is available to users on paid plans (Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans) on the web, Claude Desktop, and Claude Mobile apps. You can prompt Claude to search through your previous conversations to find relevant information across sessions and reference specific details when needed. Simply ask Claude to find what you discussed before, and it will pull together the appropriate context to keep your conversation flowing.

Memory from chat history is available for all Claude users (free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans) on the web, Claude Desktop, and Claude Mobile. Claude can now generate memory based on your chat history.
